entry.question: What is this app for?
entry.answer:
When you open an app you flagged because of an ethical problem it causes (data resale, addictive design, exploitation of workers…), a short screen asks whether you really want to open it.
It forbids nothing: it only adds a moment of reflection, so that using the app is a choice rather than a reflex.

entry.question: How do I flag an app?
entry.answer: In the Apps tab, tap an app and tick the issues that concern you. You can also start from an issue, in the Issues tab, and link several apps to it. If an issue is missing, you can add your own.

entry.question: How do I give Red Flag the permissions it needs?
entry.answer:
Red Flag needs two Android permissions: “Usage access”, to know which app opens, and “Display over other apps”, to show the interruption screen on top of it. Only you can grant them: the app cannot do it for you.
1. Tap “Agree and continue” on the last welcome screen, or tap “Grant the permissions” on the Home tab (after a short explanation). Android’s “Usage access” settings open.
2. Find “Red Flag” (on most phones the screen opens straight on it) and allow it.
3. Go back to Red Flag and tap again: Android’s “Display over other apps” settings open. Allow Red Flag the same way.
Go back to Red Flag: the Home tab shows “On” once both permissions are granted. A notification stays in the notification shade while Red Flag watches: Android requires it. You can withdraw both permissions at any time in the same places.
On some phones (Xiaomi, for example), you may also need to allow Red Flag to “display pop-up windows while running in the background” and to run without battery restrictions, in the app’s settings.

entry.question: What do the buttons on the interruption screen do?
entry.answer:
“No, close the app” takes you back to the home screen.
“Yes, open the app” opens it, and you are not asked again for 15 minutes after you last used it, even if you close the app by mistake and reopen it. The choice is forgotten earlier if the screen turns off.
The “Don’t ask again for…” link pauses the interruption for that app, for the duration set in Settings.

entry.question: Where is my data stored?
entry.answer: Everything stays on your phone: the apps you flagged, your issues, your settings and your statistics. Nothing is sent anywhere, and the app does not even request the Internet permission.

entry.question: Why does the app need usage access and to display over other apps?
entry.answer:
Usage access is what lets an app know which app has just come to the front, so that the interruption can be shown at the right moment. Displaying over other apps is what lets Red Flag open its screen at that moment, on top of the app.
Red Flag does not read what is on your screen or what you type: it only looks at the name of the app that opens, and keeps none of your usage history. You can withdraw both permissions at any time in Android’s settings.

entry.question: How do I delete my data?
entry.answer: Uninstalling the app removes everything. You can also clear its storage from Android’s settings, in the app’s information page.

entry.question: Who decides which apps are problematic?
entry.answer: You do. The app gives no verdict and keeps no list of “bad” apps: you choose, among a list of issues or your own, the ones that matter to you.

entry.question: Is this free software?
entry.answer: Yes. The app is published under the GPL v3 licence, with no advertising and no tracking.
